record.context_brief: Singular reductions of NLS and Euler
record.original_question: Find a direct reduction from the three-dimensional nonlinear Schrodinger equation to the one-dimensional nonlinear Schrodinger equation through singular solutions, and similarly relate the three-dimensional compressible Euler equation to singular solutions supported on one-dimensional submanifolds.

evidence.quote: Problem 35. Find a direct link from 3D NLS equation to 1D NLS equation as a reduction to singular solutions, rather than going through the LIA procedure. A similar question arises for the compressible Euler equations as a reduction from 3D to singular solutions supported on 1D submanifolds. Another interesting case of singular solutions is that of the vorticity supported on a hyper- surface, called a vortex sheet. One can introduce a symplectic structure on vortex sheets similar to the Marsden-Weinstein symplectic structure on membranes; see [71] for the corresponding Hamiltonian formalism. However, it is more natural to describe the motion of vortex sheets by means of a variational principle à la Arnold, albeit for a different object, as geodesics on an infinite-dimensional Lie groupoid, see Section 2.2. Using the corresponding vortex sheet groupoid instead of the group of volume-preserving diffeomorphisms in Arnold’s framework, one obtains a geometric interpretation for discontinuous fluid flows, as well as their Hamiltonian description on the corresponding dual Lie algebroid, see [59]. It turns out that vortex sheet type solutions of the Euler equation are precisely the geodesics of an L2 -type right-invariant (source-wise) metric on the Lie groupoid of discontinuous volume-preserving diffeomorphisms. The geodesics on the groupoid turn out to be weak solutions of the Euler equation with vortex sheet initial data [59]. Geometric description of vortex sheets leads to an interesting non-local metric of hydrodynam- ical pedigree on shape spaces: it is an H −1/2 -metric on closed hypersurfaces bounding the same volume (or equivalently, on constant densities inside those hypersurfaces), see [59]. Such a metric is constructed with the help of the Neumann-to-Dirichlet operators and it is always nondegenerate 27

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the three-dimensional cubic nonlinear Schrödinger (NLS) equation
   i ψ_t + Δψ + |ψ|^2 ψ = 0,   ψ : ℝ_t × ℝ^3 → ℂ,
and the one-dimensional cubic NLS equation
   i φ_t + φ_{xx} + |φ|^2 φ = 0,   φ : ℝ_t × ℝ → ℂ.

It is known that the 1D NLS arises from the dynamics of a vortex filament in ℝ^3 governed by the localized induction approximation (LIA) (the binormal flow γ_t = γ_s × γ_{ss}) via the Hasimoto transformation, which produces a 1D NLS for the complex function ψ(s,t) = κ(s,t) exp(i ∫^s τ(s',t) ds') built from the curvature κ and torsion τ of the filament.

(a) Construct a direct reduction of the 3D NLS equation to the 1D NLS equation by considering singular solutions of the 3D NLS supported on a time-dependent one-dimensional submanifold (curve) γ(·,t) ⊂ ℝ^3, expressing the resulting 1D evolution along γ as the 1D cubic NLS, without passing through the LIA / binormal flow / Hasimoto transformation.

(b) Analogously, consider the compressible Euler equations on ℝ^3 for a velocity field u and density ρ:
   ∂_t (ρ u) + ∇·(ρ u ⊗ u) + ∇p(ρ) = 0,   ∂_t ρ + ∇·(ρ u) = 0.
Construct a reduction of this 3D system to an effective one-dimensional evolution by restricting to singular solutions whose support (e.g. mass or vorticity concentration) lies on a moving one-dimensional submanifold of ℝ^3, and identify the resulting equations governing the motion of that submanifold and of the data carried along it.
artifact.category_tag: Singular solutions and vortex filament reductions
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears in a recent survey of open problems in geometric hydrodynamics (Khesin et al., ARMA 2023). Related works (e.g., the 2021 Nonlinearity paper on Hasimoto-type transforms and singular vortex membranes) note the absence of a higher-dimensional Hasimoto transform and treat the reductions via LIA rather than directly from 3D NLS or 3D Euler. No published direct reduction of 3D NLS to 1D NLS via singular solutions (bypassing LIA), nor an analogous reduction for 3D compressible Euler to singular 1D-supported solutions, appears to be available; the problem seems still open.

status_evidence.title: Hasimoto transforms and singular vortex membranes (Nonlinearity 2021)
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs LIA solutions for the Euler equation based on sphere products; notes absence of a higher-dimensional Hasimoto transform.
status_evidence.claim: Existing literature handles such reductions via LIA, not via a direct 3D-to-1D NLS reduction through singular solutions.
